Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.scenemanager.utils.run

Class RunDialogPlugin

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.scenemanager.utils.run.RunDialogPlugin
All Implemented Interfaces:
SceneManagerPlugin
public class RunDialogPlugin extends Object implements SceneManagerPlugin
The native 3D desktop's global keyboard shortcuts and its Alt+F2 "run command" dialog: the plugin counterpart of the 2D/Swing desktop's KeyEventDispatcher + RunDialog, and the first Phase-5 feature ported off the taskbar. GlassyTaskbar is not touched.

The plugin reuses the 2D desktop's pure seams rather than re-inventing them: the binding table is ShortcutMap.defaults(), resolution and recall go through RunResolver and the persisted RunHistory/RunHistoryStore, and the dialog itself is the headless-testable RunDialogPanel hosted on the HUD by RunDialog3D. Both desktops therefore share one shortcut table, one decision table and one command history.

Which shortcuts this plugin claims

Only ShortcutMap.RUN_DIALOG (Alt+F2) and ShortcutMap.OPEN_TERMINAL (Ctrl+Alt+T). The snap, show-desktop, window-close and workspace bindings in the same table are already owned by WindowSnapPlugin and WorkspacePlugin, each of which installs its own global key listener; this plugin resolves every keystroke through the shared table but acts on those two ids and deliberately ignores the rest, so the plugins never double-bind.

Why keys are dispatched programmatically, on the EDT

A hosted SwingNode only delivers KeyEvent3D to its panel while the node holds lg3d focus, which follows the pointer — but a run dialog opened by Alt+F2 must accept typing wherever the pointer is. This plugin therefore owns one global KeyEvent3D listener and, while the card is up, feeds each keystroke straight to RunDialogPanel.dispatch(java.awt.event.KeyEvent) instead of relying on AWT focus.

That listener runs on the lg3d event thread, whereas the SwingNode capture timer repaints the hosted panel on the EDT. Mutating Swing state (here, the command field) off the EDT races that repaint, so every call that touches the panel — show, hide and dispatch — is marshalled onto the EDT with SwingUtilities.invokeLater(java.lang.Runnable). A volatile showing flag is flipped synchronously on the lg3d thread so a keystroke that arrives immediately after Alt+F2 is still routed to the card rather than racing the not-yet-run show().

getPluginRoot() returns null: the card is parented to the HUD layer rather than the scene root, so it inherits the layer's perspective-compensated front pose. When DesktopHudPlugin is not running the card cannot be shown and is skipped with a warning, but Ctrl+Alt+T still opens a terminal.
